aberrant: Ab + errare: off the path. An aberrant result sticks out of the graph.
Aberrant behaviour: the polite cashier suddenly screaming. Abnormal.
abstruse: Abs + trudere (push): pushed so far away it’s hard to reach. Abstruse legal jargon.
Abstruse = “abstract and obtuse”: a physics paper no one can follow.
acerbic: Acer = sharp. Acerbic humour: lemon juice in a joke.
Un ton acerbe: a critic whose tongue cuts like vinegar.
adamant: Adamas: diamond, unbreakable. Adamant = hard as a diamond; she won’t change her mind.
Adam + ant: Adam in the garden won’t eat the apple. Firmly refuses.
admonitory: Admonish: a warning from a monitor. An admonitory finger wag.
Admonitory glance: your teacher’s look before the exam. A warning.
apocryphal: Apo + kryptein (hidden): originally hidden books. Doubtful authorship. The “Let them eat cake” line.
An apocryphal story: everyone repeats it, nobody can source it.
blatant: Loud and obvious: a blatant lie, a neon sign.
Blatant = bleating: a sheep making noise. Impossible to miss.
bumbling: Bumble + bee: knocks into everything. Mr. Bean, a bumbling fool.
Bumbling = fumbling and stumbling in a muddle.
burgeon: Bourgeon = bud. In spring, buds burgeon, so too a booming business.
Burgeon: a rapid sprouting, like a field after rain.
confound: Con + fundere (pour together): everything mixed up. The results confounded the researchers.
“Confound it!”: old-fashioned curse for bewilderment. To confuse and to contradict.
construe: Con + struere: build a meaning. You construe a text.
Misconstrue: you built the wrong meaning from his words.
contingent: Con + tangere (touch): depends on touch with another. A contingent offer: only if the buyer gets a loan.
Contingent upon rain: the picnic depends on the weather.
copious: Copia = abundance (cornucopia). Copious notes fill pages.
Un repas copieux: more than enough. Copious food.
decorum: Décorum: the formal rules. At a funeral you maintain decorum.
denigrate: Denigrate sounds like “de-nig-rate”: rate someone down, unfairly. Dénigrer.
discrete: Discrete = separate pieces, like beads on a string. Not continuous.
Discrete data vs continuous data: whole numbers only. Distinct and separate.
eradicate: E + radix (root): pull out by the root. Eradicate smallpox.
Eradicate: dig the weed out so it never returns.
espouse: Épouser: marry. You espouse a cause like a partner.
Espouse your ideas: you embrace them and take them home.
exacting: Exiger: demands accuracy. An exacting teacher marks every error.
exalt: Ex + altus (high): lift up. Exalt a hero on a pedestal.
exonerate: Ex + onus (burden): lift the burden of blame. DNA evidence exonerated the prisoner.
Exonerate: the judge says “free to go”. No longer guilty.
expound: Ex + ponere (put out): lay out in detail. A professor expounds a theory for an hour.
Expound = déployer an idea, spread it out on the table.
forthcoming: Comes forth: information freely given. A forthcoming witness answers fully.
Forthcoming also means upcoming: “the forthcoming album”.
hackneyed: Hackney horses were hired out for everyone: worn out. A hackneyed plot has been ridden too often.
Hackneyed: the cliché you’ve heard a thousand times.
iconoclastic: Adjective of iconoclast: smashing icons. An iconoclastic novel mocks every tradition.
Iconoclastic art: a painting that attacks the sacred cow.
idiosyncrasy: Idios = own: your own personal quirk. Eating pizza with a fork and knife.
Idio-syn-crasy: a mix of your own. Peculiarities.
ignoble: In + nobilis: not noble. An ignoble act of cowardice.
Ignoble = base, shameful, beneath someone of rank.
implacable: In + placare (to please): can’t be pleased or calmed. An implacable enemy.
Implacable: a storm that won’t be placated. Relentless.
implausible: Not worthy of applause (plaudere): an implausible alibi.
Implausible: a story that doesn’t pass the sniff test.
incorrigible: In + corriger: can’t be corrected. An incorrigible flirt.
Incorrigible: the kid who gets detention every week and keeps doing it.
indifference: In + differ: no difference matters. I don’t care which one.
Indifferent can also mean “mediocre”: indifferent cooking is just OK.
ingratiate: In + gratia: get into someone’s good graces. The intern ingratiates himself with the boss.
Ingratiate: flattering to win favour. S’attirer les bonnes grâces.
intransigent: In + transigere (to settle): won’t make a deal. An intransigent negotiator.
Intransigent: no transaction possible; the other side won’t move an inch.
largess: Large = generous: large-hearted gift-giving. A rich patron’s largess.
Largesse: the lord throwing coins to the crowd.
laudable: Laus = praise (applaud). A laudable effort deserves a laud.
myopic: Myopia: short-sighted. A myopic CEO only sees next quarter.
Myopic = squinting at what’s right in front and missing the horizon.
opaque: Opaque: you can’t see through it. An opaque curtain; an opaque contract.
Opaque explanations leave you in the dark.
ostentatious: Ostendere: to show off. A gold watch flashed at dinner.
Ostentatious: peacock feathers in a pastel office. Flashy.
pedantic: Pedagogue: the one who corrects every comma. A pedantic copy-editor.
Pedant: obsessed with the rules and minor details. A know-it-all.
petulant: Petulant = sulky: the toddler who throws his toy. Not « pétulant » (lively).
A petulant pout when told no. Childish bad temper.
pragmatic: Pragma = deed. A pragmatic solution works in the real world, not in theory.
Pragmatic: the engineer says “It works, ship it.”
provincial: Provincial: from the province, away from the capital. Narrow, unsophisticated views.
A provincial outlook: thinks the village is the world.
pundit: Pandit: learned scholar, now a TV expert. A political pundit has an opinion on everything.
Pundit: the “expert” paid to comment on the news.
reconcile: Re + conciliare: bring together again. The two sisters reconcile.
Reconcile accounts: both ledgers must match.
refute: Re + futare (beat back): prove wrong with evidence. Refute the accusation.
Refute: not just say “no”; show a proof that it’s false.
soporific: Sopor = deep sleep. A soporific lecture is a sleeping pill.
Soporific = sleep-making: warm room, slow voice, closed eyes.
temperance: Moderation, a cardinal virtue. Temperance movement: against alcohol.
Temper (mix) in measure: one glass, not the whole bottle.
tortuous: Torquere: twisted road. Tortuous mountain road; a tortuous explanation.
Tortuous ≠ torturous (painful): this one winds like a serpent.
underscore: Underline a word: emphasise it. The report underscores the danger.
unscrupulous: Scrupulus: a small sharp stone. The unscrupulous don’t feel the stone: no conscience.
Unscrupulous: a dealer who sells fake watches without any guilt.
